name: Eperisone Hydrochloride
sections: Developed in Japan and widely used in Asia for spastic paralysis and musculoskeletal spasm; marketed in India in IR and SR forms. First approval/introduction: Japan 1983 (Eisai).

Inhibits spinal mono- and polysynaptic reflexes and gamma-motor neuron activity, reduces muscle spindle sensitivity, and has vasodilator action that improves muscle blood flow – relieving spasticity and myotonia with little sedation. Receptor / target profile: Inhibits spinal reflexes and gamma-motor neurone activity; vasodilator action improves muscle blood flow; suppresses pain reflex.
Summary: Rapidly absorbed; Tmax 1.6–1.9 h; extensive first-pass metabolism. Half-life ~1.6–1.8 h (sustained-release prolongs action for once-daily dosing).
Muscle spasm associated with low back pain, cervical spondylosis, periarthritis of shoulder
Spastic paralysis – cerebrovascular disease, spinal cord injury, post-operative sequelae
SR 150 mg: one tablet once daily after a meal
Conventional release: 50 mg three times daily
Elderly: monitor, reduce dose if needed
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Use only if benefit outweighs risk.
LFTs and renal function on long-term use.
Chandanwale et al., J Postgrad Med 2011 – eperisone comparable to thiocolchicoside in acute low back pain with less sedation.
May cause drowsiness or weakness – caution while driving
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
